title: Fix Glossary Table Styling Issues
description:
Fix styling issues in the glossary table in print/tex/semio-table.sty:

Issues to fix:
1. First row has an offset/gap at the top that shouldn't be there
2. Text inside rows has no spacing towards the top - should have consistent vertical padding
3. Header text also lacks proper top spacing

The problems are in the `\semio@table@setup@long` command (line 105-109) where `\extrarowheight` is set to 0pt, removing all vertical spacing. Additionally, the compensation with `\\[\dimexpr-\semio@spacing@single\relax]` on line 147 is insufficient.

Solution needs to:
- Restore proper vertical spacing for long tables
- Ensure header and body rows have consistent top padding
- Remove the gap between the top border and the first row
summary:
Fixed two rounds of glossary/register/reference long-table styling issues in print/tex/semio-table.sty:

**Round 1 (vertical row padding):**
- Restored `\extrarowheight` to `\semio@spacing@single` in `\semio@table@setup@long` (was 0pt, removing all row padding).
- Removed the compensating negative vskip `\\[\dimexpr-\semio@spacing@single\relax]` from `\semio@table@long@header@repeat@three` that was fighting the padding.

**Round 2 (root-caused the remaining visual bugs after user reported they persisted):**
- The header/first-row gap was still oversized because `\semio@table@setup@long` (which sets `\extrarowheight` in `em` units via `\semio@spacing@single`) was called *before* the font was switched to the table's body font (`\semio@chrome@font@body`) inside `\semio@table@long@render`. The `em` value resolved against the wrong (larger, ambient) font size, producing an oversized gap instead of a small consistent top padding. Fixed by moving `\semio@table@setup@long` to after `\fontsize{\semio@chrome@font@body}...\selectfont`.
- The window chip/tab (e.g. "Glossar") showed a spurious bottom border, making it look like a fully enclosed box instead of an open tab merging into the table below. Root cause: the leading `\hline` right after `\begin{longtable}{#1}` in `\semio@table@long@render` spanned the *entire* table width, including underneath the chip, duplicating/extending the border that the window chrome's own `\semio@window@header@gap@paint` bottom stroke already draws (correctly, only from the chip's right edge onward). Fixed by removing that leading `\hline` — the chip's own gap-paint stroke (aligned via the existing `-\semio@stroke@hairline` vskip) now provides the sole top border, starting exactly at the chip's bottom-right corner.

Verified visually by rendering an isolated minimal test document (`verify-glossary.tex`, based on the existing PRINT-GLOSSARY-MECHANISM ticket's test fixture) to PNG at high resolution — confirmed the chip has no bottom border, the table's top border starts at the chip's right edge, and the header-to-first-row gap is now a small, consistent padding matching other rows.

Note: full builds of the shared print templates (report, zwischenbericht) were intermittently broken during this session by an unrelated, actively-in-progress change to print/tex/semio-window.sty (a `WindowArrangement`/`WindowColumn` feature under concurrent development in another session, tracked separately). Verification was done via an isolated TEXINPUTS override that bypassed only that in-progress region, without touching the shared file.
